A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a simple and rationally based strength model for predicting the debonding failures of FRP and steel plate end debonded RC beams, which is suitable for use in design.
the model is simple, rationally-based and easy to use.
the plate end debonded failure load is governed by the shear capacity of a beam, and the debonding length and the shear capacity of an FRP or a steel plate are not critical.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear capacity of a beam is the key to predicting the strength of plate end debonded beams.
plate end debonded failure is governed by shear and that it can be predicted by using shear strength of the concrete and a simple shear friction model for the bond.
plate end debondings in RC beams are governed primarily by shear, rather than flexure.
